proposed.explanation: Your situation calls for converting your TMGH holding into cash as soon as possible. You need 40,000 EGP within 2 months to pay your child's university fees, and your entire portfolio (2,000 EGP cash + 300 × 82.50 = 24,750 EGP in TMGH) is only worth 26,750 EGP. You are already 13,250 EGP short of the amount you need, so you cannot afford to leave any capital exposed to stock-price risk over the next two months. Your risk tolerance is low in both willingness and ability, and a 2-month horizon is too short to rely on the stock's fundamental strength to protect your capital. While the FY2025 results show solid growth (net profit rose from 12,769,517,325 LE to 18,201,981,482 LE; EPS from 4.38 to 6.98 LE), that does not guarantee the share price will hold or rise over the next 60 days. Selling all 300 shares at the current 82.50 EGP gives you 24,750 EGP in cash, bringing your total liquid funds to 26,750 EGP. You will still need to find the remaining 13,250 EGP from another source (savings, family support, a short-term loan, etc.) to meet the 40,000 EGP deadline. This is not a judgment on TMGH's long-term quality; it is a liquidity and risk-management decision driven by your hard 2-month deadline and very low capacity for loss. There is uncertainty in any short-term price move, but locking in the current value removes that uncertainty from an obligation you cannot miss.

claims.statement: TMGH consolidated net profit for FY2025 was 18,201,981,482 LE.
TMGH consolidated net profit for FY2024 (restated) was 12,769,517,325 LE.
TMGH consolidated EPS for FY2025 was 6.98 LE.
TMGH consolidated EPS for FY2024 (restated) was 4.38 LE.

limitations: The evidence covers only FY2025 and FY2024 consolidated results; there is no forward guidance, no interim 2026 data, and no information on upcoming dividends, buybacks, or sector-specific risks that could affect the share price over the next two months.

The 40,000 EGP liquidity need exceeds the total portfolio value (26,750 EGP), so even a full liquidation will not cover the obligation; the investor must identify an additional 13,250 EGP from outside the portfolio.
Share prices can move in either direction over a 2-month window; the current 82.50 EGP price is the only reference point available and may differ at the time of execution.
